lines: The testament dative and inventar of the guidis geir soumes of
money and debtis perteining to umquhile John Glasgow in Quodquen within the
parochin of Libbertoun and sheriffdome of Lanark the tyme of his deceis
quha deceist in the moneth of [illegible] the yeir of God 1661 yeiris
faithfullie maid and givin up be Thomas Glasgow [descriptor illegible]
in name of executour dative [appointment wording illegible]
James Hamiltoun commissar of Lanark [confirmation formula continuing]
[the said] John Glasgow [following descriptor and grammatical subject unresolved]
[administration, caution, and closing formula partly illegible]

plain_english: This is the testament dative and inventory of John Glasgow in Quothquan, Libberton parish, Lanarkshire. It places his death in 1661 but the month remains unreadable.

Thomas Glasgow is readable in the giver-up/executor-dative passage. The ink immediately after his name does not securely read 'lawful son', and the page-break continuation does not safely establish its grammatical subject.
James Hamilton is the commissary confirming the estate. His presence is official rather than familial.
No parent-child relationship is created from Thomas's participation or from the later occurrence of John Glasgow in the legal continuation.
findings: Newly improved reading: Thomas Glasgow can be named in the giver-up/executor-dative context, but his exact capacity and descriptor remain unresolved.
Excluded reading: the marks after Thomas and around the page-break occurrence of John do not prove 'lawful son'.
Confirmed: deceased John Glasgow lived in Quodquen within Libberton parish and the sheriffdom of Lanark and died in 1661.
Confirmed: James Hamilton acts as commissary of Lanark, not as executor or kin.
The 1661/1662 John is kept distinct from the 1650 and 1685 Quothquan Johns unless another record bridges them.
changes_from_previous: The previous review left the giver-up wholly unnamed. This reread promotes Thomas Glasgow as a probable-to-secure personal-name reading while retaining brackets around his descriptor and exact executorial capacity.
The former proposed sonship remains rejected: neither proximity nor expected confirmation wording substitutes for visible kinship ink.
No WikiTree identity is assigned from name and locality alone.
unresolved: The words immediately following Thomas Glasgow and whether Thomas personally held the executor-dative office or acted in another representative capacity
The grammatical subject and descriptor around the page-break occurrence of John Glasgow
Inventory goods, values, debtors, creditors, totals, cautioner, and closing names
A secure WikiTree match or relationship to either the 1650 or 1685 John
confidence_statement: High for the deceased's name, Quodquen/Libberton locality, 1661 death year, entry boundaries, and James Hamilton's office. Moderate for the name Thomas Glasgow. Low for Thomas's following descriptor and any claimed sonship; no kinship is asserted.
